_readme: Narration delivery for the pilot (generate_story_audio.py). Settled by ear 2026-08: the plain voice at 128k mp3 with no speed adjustment and no emotion sounded clean, while 96k / a speed adjustment / the emotion parameter (in some combination) made it nasal and watery — so those stay off until re-tested one at a time with --diagnose. Sentence pauses at 250ms were picked from --pause-test. Resolution order for every setting is age_bands > tellers > top level, so a band can override pace or even voice while tellers still choose who is telling. Every band the library may contain has an entry, including 3-4 and 11-12 which have no stories yet — otherwise a new band would silently inherit the 9-10 pacing. Younger bands get longer pauses rather than slower speech, because pauses cost nothing in audio quality and a speed adjustment is exactly what we suspect of the artifacts — revisit with `--diagnose` at 128k before adding speed back. Paragraph and segment gaps are NOT here: they're player-side (BujuPilot.narration in pilot/js/stories.js) and are themselves scaled per age band, so they retune without regenerating. Anything in this file is baked into the mp3s: change it and regenerate with --force. 2026-08 update: the 3-4 band was the first to be voiced and the first listened to by a parent, and it came back 'too fast and too harsh'. The cause was that younger bands only ever got longer PAUSES — every word was still delivered at speed 1.0 — so a three-year-old's story was fast bursts separated by 550ms of silence, which reads as staccato rather than gentle. 3-4 now slows the words (speed 0.92) and shortens the gaps to 400ms so it flows instead of stuttering. 0.85 was tried first and was audibly nasal, confirming the long-standing suspicion about this knob: sonic-3's speed adjustment degrades the voice, and the degradation scales with how far from 1.0 you push it. Treat speed as a small trim, not as the way to get a gentle read — for that, pick a voice that is natively slow and warm and leave speed alone. If the words sound watery at 0.85, that is the artifact this file has always suspected of the speed knob: back off toward 0.9 and re-check with --diagnose at 128k rather than reverting to 1.0. LANGUAGES (2026-08): `languages` maps a language code to the voice that reads it. Resolution for voice_id is languages > age_bands > tellers > top level — a story narrated in Hindi uses the Hindi voice whatever its teller says, because teller is about who is telling, not what language they speak. Pace still resolves by band. English is listed explicitly so the default is visible rather than implied. A language here is only half the job: the story also needs a `translations.<lang>` block, or there is nothing for the voice to read — a voice does not translate.
